Publish soil-health scores

Source: R/publish-health.R
soil_publish_health.Rd

Publishes the soil-health scores computed by an external model in an open run of a product version that declares one or more of the variables soil_health_physical_score, soil_health_chemical_score, soil_health_soc_score. Each score is one horizon and one category; the API publishes the generic value and the soil-health details in one transaction.

Usage

soil_publish_health(
  soil = soil_session(),
  run_id,
  scores,
  idempotency_key,
  transport = c("auto", "sync", "ndjson"),
  wait = TRUE,
  timeout = 3600,
  poll = 5,
  progress = interactive()
)

Arguments

soil

A session; the default session when omitted. Client-side: not sent to the API.

run_id

The id of an open run. API path parameter {run_id} of POST /publications/{run_id}/values, /validate and /jobs (for soil_publish_health(): /soil-health and /soil-health/jobs).

scores

A data frame (list columns for nested fields) or a list of records with horizon_id, release_id, category_code (e.g. "physical"), score_status ("scored", "insufficient_data", "not_applicable"), score, score_class, source_support ("observed_point_profile", "polygon_estimate", "map_unit_profile_relation", "non_spatial_profile", "non_spatial_estimate"), and optionally quality_code, observation_inputs (list of list(observation_id =, input_role =, required =, transformation =)), value_inputs, release_inputs, asset_inputs (lists of list(id =, role =)), inputs, derived_variables, memberships, diagnostics (named lists) and activated_rules (list of named lists). API field scores; with the NDJSON transport, the lines of the file sent as API form field file.

idempotency_key

Key of this publication (at most 200 characters), stable for one content. API field idempotency_key of a synchronous publication; API query parameter idempotency_key of an NDJSON upload.

transport

"auto" (synchronous up to 10,000 records, else NDJSON), "sync" or "ndjson". Client-side: not sent to the API.

wait

For a job: wait for it to end (see soil_job_wait()). Client-side: not sent to the API.

timeout, poll

Seconds to wait for a job, and between two polls. Client-side: not sent to the API.

progress

Print the progress of the job. Client-side: not sent to the API.

Value

A soil_publication list as soil_publish_values(), with score_count for a synchronous publication.

Details

Local checks of every record before anything is sent: required fields (horizon_id a UUID, release_id, category_code, score_status, source_support), allowed score_status and source_support, score and class consistency (a scored record has a numeric score and a score_class; any other status has neither), observation inputs with an observation_id (UUID) and an input_role, and no duplicate horizon, category and release. Problems are a soilhub_argument_error whose errors lists them by record.

Up to 10,000 records are published synchronously (POST /publications/{run_id}/soil-health; a rejected batch is a soilhub_validation_error with the API's errors); above, or with transport = "ndjson", an NDJSON file with its SHA-256 checksum is uploaded as a job (POST /publications/{run_id}/soil-health/jobs), never repeated automatically. The same idempotency_key with the same content returns the first receipt; any difference, even only in the memberships, rules or diagnostics, is a soilhub_conflict_error (HTTP 409): use a new key. The receipt is reconciled with the records sent (published_count, score_count): a difference is a soilhub_reconciliation_warning.

Rights: soil:publish. Capabilities: publish_soil_health_sync (synchronous), bulk_soil_health (job).

See also

Other writing: soil_product(), soil_product_version(), soil_publish_source(), soil_publish_values(), soil_register_variable(), soil_run_open(), soil_source_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
scores <- list(list(
  horizon_id = "4fa5fbe3-8fd4-4fb1-94cf-d07963eb50f7", release_id = 12L,
  category_code = "physical", score_status = "scored", score = 72.5,
  score_class = "good", source_support = "polygon_estimate",
  observation_inputs = list(list(
    observation_id = "46f252f1-5f38-4223-b329-88822f60fe75",
    input_role = "bulk_density", transformation = "membership_low_compaction"
  )),
  inputs = list(bulk_density = 1.31),
  memberships = list(poor = 0.1, moderate = 0.3, good = 0.8),
  activated_rules = list(list(rule = "physical_r4", strength = 0.7))
))
soil_publish_health(soil, run$run_id, scores, "fuzzy-v1-india-2026-10")
} # }
